title: [Peek] Minimum window size is defined inconsistently in XAML and code

judgment.rationale: The conflicting definitions are confirmed in source, but active maintainer work and an upcoming WASDK API require coordination before implementation.
evidence: The issue gives a mixed-DPI size failure and links related Peek scaling issues.
The assignee says a broader fix is forthcoming; a maintainer mentions new WASDK sizing APIs.
judgment.recommended_action: Coordinate with the active Peek maintainer solution, then approve a single-source DPI-aware design.

fix_assessment.rationale: No merged or open concrete fix PR covering this issue was found; comments describe planned work but not a published implementation.

issue_context.summary: Peek has two minimum-size sources: XAML sets 480x320 DIPs while WindowConstants.cs exposes 500x500 values used by runtime sizing. The issue and discussion identify mixed-DPI/cross-display calculations and an upcoming WASDK API.
known_information: Issue is open and assigned to daverayment.
The report gives a 512x512 image opening at 820x586 on a 175% display.
Discussion mentions new WASDK minimum-size APIs and an active broader solution.
inferences: The discrepancy is a real unit/source-of-truth defect.
Runtime minimums and the 80% safe zone must be reconciled together.
issue_context.analysis: The public report names exact files and values and source confirms both definitions. The design must preserve DPI and cross-monitor behavior and coordinate with active maintainer work.
initial_investigation: Read WindowConstants.cs and MainWindow.xaml on main.
Read the complete discussion including the WASDK note and the assignee's planned scaling solution.
Checked related #50193 and #50244 as scaling work, not duplicates.

information_gaps.information: Which minimum-size API and unit convention the maintainer solution will standardize on
information_gaps.why_needed: Prevents a competing design from being superseded by planned WASDK work
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm target Windows App SDK API/version and physical-pixel versus DIP contract

proposed_fixes.title: Unify Peek minimum sizing in one DPI-aware path
proposed_fixes.root_cause: XAML and runtime sizing use separate values and units: 480x320 DIPs versus 500x500 runtime values.
plan: Convert once at the WinUI/Win32 boundary using active monitor scale.
Apply it to runtime and XAML/WASDK constraints.
verification: Open square and rectangular images at mixed DPI.
Drag Peek between displays and reopen after display changes.
Verify the 80% safe-zone rule still wins when minimum cannot fit.

confidence.rationale: Conflicting constants and units are confirmed, but active maintainer work and API choice remain.

design.root_cause: Peek defines MinWidth/MinHeight in XAML as 480x320 DIPs and separately uses 500x500 runtime constants.
evidence: The issue supplies a 175% DPI example and links cross-display issues.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Runtime code consumes 500x500 independently from XAML minima.
implementation_steps.change: Make one canonical DIP or physical-pixel minimum contract explicit.
implementation_steps.code_block: public const double MinWindowWidthDip = 480; public const double MinWindowHeightDip = 320;

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Runtime auto-size and Win32 minimum handling can use a different unit space than XAML.
implementation_steps.change: Convert canonical minima once using active scale and apply them consistently with safe-zone calculations.
implementation_steps.code_block: var minPx = DipToPhysical(canonicalMinDip, monitorScale); minWidth = Math.Min(minPx.Width, safeZone.Width);

verify: Build Peek projects and run focused sizing tests.
Reproduce the 512x512 image at 175% and cross-display transitions.
risks: Future WASDK APIs may replace part of the design.
alternatives: Change only XAML; runtime remains inconsistent.
Change only runtime constants; XAML remains a second source.

comment.body: The live source still has 480x320 DIPs in MainWindow.xaml and 500x500 runtime constants in WindowConstants.cs. The discussion mentions an upcoming WASDK minimum-size API and a broader maintainer fix. Please confirm the target API/version and canonical unit contract so implementation does not conflict with that planned work.
